correctness.rationale: For a binary five-dimensional projective multiset, the subspace correspondence gives \(d_3=n-L\), \(d_4=n-M\), and the CEZ containment condition gives \(g_4=n-B\). Under a strict gap \(B<M\), a maximum-multiplicity point lies on no maximum-mass line. If \(b\) is the largest point multiplicity on a maximum line, the line through that point and a global maximum point is nonmaximal, so \(L\ge M+b+1\), while the binary maximum line has three points and \(L\le3b\). Hence \(M\ge3\). Rank five requires two further positive points outside the three-dimensional vector span of the maximum point and maximum line, giving \(n\ge M+L+2\ge11\). The explicit length-eleven multiset has \(M=3,L=6,B=2\), so \(d_4=8,g_4=9\). Exact replay independently gives hierarchy \((1,2,5,8,11)\) and directly computes \(g_4=9\) from the CEZ definition.

value.rationale: The primary September 2026 paper makes the fourth greedy gap in five-dimensional codes a current optimization problem. An exact first-occurrence threshold is a natural complementary invariant: it identifies the smallest binary ambient code on which the phenomenon can exist at all. The proof is structural rather than a table search, and the length-eleven construction is sharp. This converts a large-parameter gap-optimization program into a compact binary boundary theorem.
